title: Managing variants
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
A project can contain multiple variants or scenarios. Variants store input configurations that can be loaded, edited and recalculated individually. The workflow is create/define → save/load → simulate → compare.

title: Managing variants
text:
Comparing variants deliberately
First save a traceable reference. Create variants changing individual parameters or related measures, such as PV sizing or heat supply. This helps identify which change causes a difference.
Meaningful comparison requires aligned boundaries, reference areas, time bases and methods. Record tool version and calculation state. See variant comparison for evaluation.

title: Managing variants
text:
Creating and saving a variant

Where in PEExcel?

Set project and variant names, clearly distinguishing baseline and measure.
Configure inputs on technical sheets and calculate.
Invoke Aktuelle Eingabe speichern (save current inputs) and assign the intended project.
Before confirming, check whether you are creating a new variant or overwriting an existing one.

title: Managing variants
text:
Loading a saved variant
Select the project and variant in the manager and load it. Check names and loaded inputs; recalculate after changes or if results are out of date. Save unsaved changes before switching variants.

title: Managing variants
text:
Continuing work
Presets help configure inputs. Migration transfers projects to new versions. Use comparison for analysis and batch simulation for many variants.
Source: Training, slides 28 and 33 (German).

title: Storage and flexibility
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
Energy flexibility connects the timing of renewable energy availability with district operation. Local PV surpluses and external flexibility signals can enable additional conditioning and storage charging. Minimum-demand coverage and flexible additional supply remain separate quantities.

title: Storage and flexibility
text:
How storage options work together



Interaction of heat pumps, thermal building mass, stationary batteries and pooled electric mobility. When enabled, usable storage is charged; outside the enabled period it can meet demand. This illustrates the principle, not a universal operating schedule.


The model distinguishes two signal types for flexible operation:

Local PV surpluses indicate that locally generated PV electricity is available for additional applications.
An external enable signal permits flexible operation based on an external time series. The signal supplied with the tool is based on wind-power surpluses in Austria. For your own investigations, external enable signals can also be derived from other sources, such as hourly CO₂ intensities.

The district’s flexibility potentials determine how an enable signal can be used. Actual energy uptake depends on available surplus or import, system capacity and storage state.  | Flexibility potential | What happens? | What limits use? | What shows the effect? | |—|—|—|—| | Thermal building mass | Heating or cooling temporarily increases | Effective thermal mass, comfort band and system capacity | Room temperature and subsequent heating/cooling demand | | Hot-water storage | Additional heating of the buffer/storage tank | Volume, upper temperature and charging capacity | Storage state, charging and losses | | Stationary battery | Electricity is stored and used later | Capacity, C-rate and efficiencies | SoC, charging, discharging and full cycles | | Electric vehicles | Flexible charging; district supply when enabled | Presence, charging points, power and minimum SoC | Charging flows and SoC by use |
Minimum supply remains part of the simulation. Flexible charging uses additional available headroom. A high enabled-time share alone says little about the energy actually shifted.

title: Storage and flexibility
text:
Enable settings and sources

Where in PEExcel? Check PV-surplus use and Signal verwenden (use signal) separately. Specify which applications may use the signal and their power limits. Presets provide an initial selection; actual switches and parameters are decisive.

Configure generation on the PV page. Track conventional grid import, flexible grid import and self-consumption separately in the results.

title: Storage and flexibility
text:
Thermal building mass
Additional electric heating or cooling can use building mass as storage. The selected system and permitted departure from the temperature setpoint determine preconditioning. Set construction type or effective thermal mass on 🧱 Bauphysik; see building physics.

Comfort band and system selection
These fields define the permissible departure from the room-temperature setpoint during flexible conditioning.

title: Storage and flexibility
text:
Hot-water storage
Flexible heating temporarily raises the temperature of existing storage. Check activation and upper temperature. Size, baseline supply and losses belong to the hot-water configuration.

A higher temperature creates additional headroom but may increase storage losses. Check the Excel dashboard to see whether the additional charge is effectively used.

title: Storage and flexibility
text:
Electric battery
Define activation, energy capacity, charge/discharge power, efficiencies and self-discharge together. Capacity in kWh and power in kW are different quantities. The source of charging and use of discharge determine the effects on imports and feed-in. C-rate connects power and capacity: 20 kWh at 0.5 h⁻¹ corresponds to a maximum of 10 kW.

title: Storage and flexibility
text:
Electric vehicles
Flexible charging and bidirectional use depend on parking periods, charging power, capacity and minimum state of charge (SoC). Enter these on 🚗 Mobilität; see the mobility model.

title: Storage and flexibility
text:
Dynamic assessment



Method: imports, exports and time-dependent assessment of energy carriers. Source: PEExcel training.


Hourly conversion factors assess energy use over time. Report physical savings, temporal shifts and improvements in an assessed balance separately.






NoteResearch / Expert





Set hourly conversion factors on sheet ⚖️ and enter the corresponding enable signals on 🚦 Signale (signals). On 🔋 Flexibilität und Speicher (storage and flexibility), specify which applications may use the signal and their power limits.
To investigate CO₂-dependent control, derive an enable signal from an hourly CO₂-intensity series, for example by enabling hours below a chosen threshold, and enter that signal. Document the data source, unit, time reference and threshold. Conversion factors and enable signals must refer to the same hours.
The enable signal permits flexible operation within the configured limits. Conversion factors assess the resulting energy use. Compare a reference and the signal-controlled variant using energy imports, storage states and assessed emissions. Apply the separate requirements for a declaration.




Declaration: Use the designated requirements for enable settings, capacities and conversion factors. Free modelling assumptions are possible but do not automatically establish compliance.

Analyse flexibility step by step
Result checks: Evaluate annual indicators together with hourly flows and storage states.
Source: Training, slides 9, 15 and 21 (German). Comfort-band and hot-water examples come from the supplied KlimSta slide “Building as Battery, thermische Speicher Gebäude”.

title: Results and indicators
text:
Available indicators
Browse all OUT variables: units, labels and assignments from the active schema, including costs, flexibility and storage.
Annual results complement hourly charts. Keep indicator, reference area and balance boundary consistent when comparing.








Area
Indicators
Interpretation




Buildings
Heating/cooling demand, heat gains and losses
Distinguish annual energy from power and temperature


Electricity
Demand, grid import, PV use and feed-in
Read local supply separately from external mobility charging


PV self-consumption
Direct, flexible and total shares
Share of PV generation assigned to the respective local uses


Energy autonomy
Local direct and flexible PV use relative to electricity demand
A PV-related indicator, not supply security or islanding capability


Grid feed-in
Peak PV export in kW and its timestamp
Maximum on an hourly basis; no statement about shorter peaks or grid voltages


Stationary battery
Annual charge/discharge, losses, round-trip efficiency, equivalent full cycles
Assess use and losses together; full cycles alone do not determine service life


Flexibility
Annual and summer/winter enabled-time shares, flexible grid and PV use
Enablement is an opportunity; actual use depends on demand and storage state


Mobility
Distance travelled, electric/fossil destination-traffic demand, EV charging and full cycles
Generated traffic and physical charging have different boundaries


Assessment
Primary energy, operational/embodied GHG contributions, total balance and distance to budget
Assessed quantities complement physical flows




Self-consumption and energy autonomy
The PV self-consumption share divides direct plus flexible local PV use by PV generation. Energy autonomy uses the same numerator but total electricity demand as denominator. Higher PV yield can affect these two shares differently.
When comparing tools, align definitions, including mobility and storage charging. The same term, such as “self-sufficiency”, does not guarantee the same boundary.

title: Results and indicators
text:
Project indicators
Check project/variant name, areas, use mix, development density, and cooled and mechanically ventilated shares. Note whether each balance refers to net floor area (NGF) or gross floor area (BGF).

title: Results and indicators
text:
Heat balance
Charts compare transmission and ventilation losses, night ventilation, solar and internal gains, and heating/cooling demand. Read the whole district, cooled and uncooled areas, and heating/cooling periods separately. Heating and cooling capacities are power quantities, not annual energy.

title: Results and indicators
text:
Final-energy balance
The demand–supply matrix assigns user electricity, building services, hot water, storage charging and mobility to supply sources. Row and column sums make energy use traceable. Read imports, local use, storage flows and feed-in within their boundaries; do not indiscriminately add them.

title: Results and indicators
text:
Flexibility and battery
Enabled periods, flexible use, battery charge/discharge, losses and cycles describe how available potential is used. Annual indicators complement the dashboard’s time-resolved analysis.

title: Results and indicators
text:
Primary-energy balance
Demand and supply are assessed using conversion factors. Local renewables and flexible imports appear as substitution equivalents; context factors account for development density, refurbishment and mobility. The import/export presentation covers exchange across the district boundary. Read each presentation using its own signs and system boundary.

title: Results and indicators
text:
GHG balance
Construction and operational contributions, including mobility, are shown cumulatively. Emissions, credits, budget and balance are separate quantities. Check assessment period and gross-floor-area reference. LCA inputs and verification are documented separately.
Variant comparison · Excel dashboard · Real website examples
Source: Training, slides 21–25; interface structure follows manual pp. 74–82 (German).

title: Results and indicators
text:
Common concept-design questions

Are variant comparison and sensitivity studies already available?
Yes. Save inputs as variants, calculate individually or by batch, and evaluate in variant comparison. For example, compare storage sizes and C-rates with the same building and PV system. Variants are deliberately specified; this is not automatic optimisation.


What time resolution is available?
The annual simulation uses 8,760 hours. Daily, monthly and annual evaluations aggregate these results. A 15-minute model would require adapted input data and calculation methods; splitting an hourly value into four equal intervals adds no temporal information.


Can grid relief be assessed?
Hourly import/export profiles and peak feed-in support comparison of district exchange. Transformer loading, voltage limits and individual feeders require an additional grid model. Lower annual imports alone do not demonstrate relief at the critical grid hour.


How are CO₂ savings determined?
Compare a reference and a measure variant with the same assessment boundary. Distinguish operational and life-cycle balances, using the same factors, periods and areas. If factors or signals change, report their effects explicitly, as in the flexibility example.


Are economics, resilience and permitting covered?
The results structure contains cost fields for grid import, flexible import and feed-in. This does not establish a complete investment or life-cycle cost analysis. Check tariff assumptions and output completeness for economic evaluation. Grid-outage resilience, fire safety and permitting require additional criteria and studies.


What data does a use case need?
Start with location, areas and uses, envelope properties, supply, PV, storage and mobility assumptions. Presets support initial concepts; replace key assumptions with project-specific data afterwards. Comparison with operation benefits from time-aligned measurements of consumption, generation, grid exchange and, ideally, storage states. Data interfaces distinguish concept and validation data.

title: Project verification
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
The klimaaktiv standard can be applied at different project stages. Distinguish two questions: Which quality level is achieved in the calculation? And how robust is the underlying project status? The standard describes quality levels; the declaration phase identifies the stage of verification.

title: Project verification
text:
Three declaration phases
Verification can take place during design, after completion and using measured operational data. As the project progresses, the data basis and the declaration’s significance change.






Figure 1: Declaration according to project status: design, completion and operation, with increasing availability of as-built and measured data.




📐 Design declaration — demonstrating potential and variants
A design declaration recognises a well-founded investigation of a district concept. It shows under which planning, technical and organisational conditions a target quality level could be achieved. Especially early on, it supports what-if questions: How much PV area would be needed? Which heat supply or mobility measures would make the difference? How strongly do construction types affect the GHG balance?
The studied variant does not have to be implemented exactly as assessed. A design declaration is neither a commitment to build that variant nor proof of subsequent actual performance. What matters is a sufficiently detailed, traceable investigation and transparent identification of assumptions and dependencies.


🏗️ Completion declaration — checking implementation
The completion declaration assesses the district actually built or refurbished. Compare design measures with the as-built state: envelope, installed heat generation, available PV areas and capacities, storage, charging infrastructure and implemented mobility services.
Document deviations from earlier variants and reassess them where relevant to the balance. The basis is evidenced construction and the resulting calculated target achievement, not merely the original design result.


🔍 Operational or monitoring declaration — demonstrating performance in use
The operational declaration supplements model-based assessment with measured operational data from at least one year of monitoring. Compare energy imports, generation and feed-in, and further flows and operating conditions where measurable and relevant to the quality level, with assessment assumptions.
Sound interpretation considers weather, occupancy, changes in use and technical-system availability. Monitoring identifies differences between predicted and actual performance. It does not replace assessment of life-cycle or mobility emissions that cannot be measured directly.



Table 1: Assessment basis and significance of declaration phases.










Phase
Assessment basis
What the declaration establishes




📐 Design
District concept, technical assumptions and investigated variants
Conditions under which a quality level is achievable


🏗️ Completion
Evidenced construction and updated calculation
Whether the implemented project meets requirements


🔍 Operation / monitoring
Measurements and documented operating conditions
The extent to which predicted performance is confirmed in operation












WarningCaution



Quality level describes the scope of energy and GHG requirements met. Declaration phase indicates whether assessment uses design assumptions, actual construction or measured operation. These are independent and must be reported together.

title: Project verification
section: 🧭 “On the way” — reaching the target in stages
text:
🧭 “On the way” — reaching the target in stages
Not every district meets all requirements for its intended quality level at the time of verification. Particularly in existing districts or phased development, important measures may take effect later.
The declaration “Auf dem Weg zum Plus-Energie-Quartier” (“On the way to a positive energy district”) accounts for such pathways where later achievement within the intended period can be demonstrated plausibly. The concept provides a period of up to five years.
Distinguish a general intention from a technically and temporally credible implementation pathway. Suitable evidence may include:

Reserved PV areas: secured roof or façade areas, including load capacity, shading, cable routes and future connection.
Prepared energy flexibility: metering, control and communication infrastructure plus an implementable control concept.
Technical provisions: conduits, space, routes or electrical connection reserves for expansion.
Traceable stages: specific measures, responsibilities, prerequisites and implementation dates.

Such a pathway does not prove a quality level has already been achieved. Present the current state and intended complete achievement separately.
GHG assessment must also include emissions before later implementation and additional manufacturing emissions of the measures. A good future result does not undo emissions already incurred.
See LCA for refurbishment and life-cycle assessment.

Declaration: Binding conditions for “On the way”, particularly deadlines, evidence and quality-level assignment, follow the applicable declaration requirements.

title: Project verification
text:
Verification process
A network of the contact point, competence partners and expert panel supports the path to klimaaktiv recognition. For project owners, the process has three steps.






Figure 2: Your path to a positive energy district: initial minimum-requirement checks, selection of professional project support, submission and quality assurance.




Step 1 — check minimum requirements and prospects
First clarify the project’s basic prerequisites and prospects of a successful declaration. A PED Quick Check can provide an initial assessment.
Discuss possible concept adjustments, outstanding requirements and a suitable timetable. The Anlaufstelle Plus-Energie-Quartiere contact point supports this initial orientation.


Step 2 — select a competence partner
Project owners can select a klimaaktiv competence partner for detailed work.
Together, define project scope, boundaries, variants and the services required. These may include data collection, calculation, technical advice and preparation of declaration documents.
Competence partners support application of the standard and traceable preparation of evidence.


Step 3 — submission and quality assurance
Once project support is complete, submit the required results and documents for professional review.
The klimaaktiv expert panel checks verification and may ask about assumptions, calculations or evidence. Successful review leads to the corresponding declaration or recognition.
Quality assurance supports technical plausibility, traceability and consistent application of the standard.

title: Project verification
text:
Participants and responsibilities
Verification is embedded in the klimaaktiv settlements and districts programme. Participants have different, coordinated roles.






Figure 3: The klimaaktiv programme team: contact point, settlements and districts team, competence partners and expert panel, working with project owners and technical designers.




PED contact point: initial information, advice on applicability and verification questions.
klimaaktiv settlements and districts: programme coordination and support for quality-assurance and advisory structures.
klimaaktiv competence partners: project advice, assessment and support preparing evidence.
klimaaktiv expert panel: technical quality assurance and review of submitted results.
Project owners and technical designers: project development, data provision, implementation and evidence documentation.

Cooperation should enable traceable assessment while keeping responsibilities for design, calculation and quality assurance distinct.

title: Project verification
text:
Data quality and traceability
Verification combines architecture, building physics, building services, mobility planning and LCA. For influential inputs, identify reference assumptions, project-specific calculations, confirmed as-built information or measurements. Make dependencies on unsecured measures visible.
Keep district boundary, uses, area references and assessment version consistent in variant comparisons. If these change, identify their effects on demand, context factors and allocated budgets.

title: Mobility
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
Distinguish physical charging flows from causation-based assessment. Both matter, but answer different questions.

title: Mobility
text:
Which mobility is attributed?
The method considers responsibility for generated mobility. Destination traffic and an allocated national budget reference belong to this perspective. On-site charging energy is therefore not automatically identical to total attributed mobility energy.



Mobility balance: destination traffic and other traffic by use. Source: PEExcel training.





Mobility model and balance relationships.


Source: docs/mobilität.png; training, slides 17–20. The training cites Österreich unterwegs 2014 as a data source. Assumptions and declaration values belonging to the tool version remain decisive.

title: Mobility
section: From inputs to hourly vehicle groups
text:
From inputs to hourly vehicle groups
The model connects statistical floor-area occupancy and travel data with EV share, vehicle density and use-specific simultaneity. It creates vehicle groups for housing, work and shopping, tracking presence and average states of charge throughout the year.







Input or data basis
Meaning in the model




Usable floor area and statistical occupancy
Expected number of mobile people by use


Mean distance travelled per person and location
Annual travel demand; mobility measures can change it


EV share and vehicle density
Electric share and number of assigned vehicles


Simultaneity factors
Relationship between statistical use and actual participants


Presence profiles
Hourly vehicle shares on site, off site, departing and arriving


Charging points, power and battery capacity
Technical limits on transferable energy


Minimum charge levels
Boundary between necessary charging and flexible headroom






Hourly presence profiles for one week: housing in orange at the bottom, work in blue in the middle, shopping in purple at the top. Red indicates departures, green arrivals.


Hourly convention: Departing vehicles remain present during the current hour and may charge before leaving. Arriving vehicles remain outside until the end of that hour. Profiles describe expected shares of a vehicle group, not individual schedules.
The data basis includes statistical mobility surveys, travel-distance literature and assumptions about EV shares and simultaneity. Charging/discharging responds to local PV and regional enable signals. The hourly e-mobility research example explains the derivation.

title: Mobility
text:
Where does charging actually happen?
For the energy system, what matters is when vehicles charge on site, their charging demand and interaction with PV, the grid and storage where applicable. This perspective considers the charging and traffic flows assumed in the model.

title: Mobility
text:
Comparing with a clear question
Investigate mobility concepts while keeping the building model unchanged. Record location assumptions, travel distance, transport modes and charging concept. Evaluate mobility assessment and physical electricity balance separately.






NoteResearch / Expert





Charging location alone does not determine causation-based allocation. Physical charging and assessment balances have different system boundaries. The tool’s documented allocation is decisive.



Winter and summer mobility behaviour · Results and indicators

title: Mobility
text:
Mobility in Excel

Where in PEExcel? 🚗 Mobilität.

The training distinguishes actual potential use from causation-based responsibility. Storage and load-flow simulation considers EVs travelling in the district and their charging. The assessment allocates generated destination traffic, both electric and fossil.

Select private motorised transport (MIV) modelling and calculation method. Check location, mobility measures, statistical MIV scaling, EV share and charging points. For actual charging, set capacities, efficiencies, internal/external minimum charge levels and, where applicable, bidirectional charging. After calculation, check mobility contributions on the results sheet and EV charge levels in the dashboard.

Location, parking spaces, alternative mobility services and charging infrastructure are different measures. Do not equate physical district charging with attributed mobility demand.
Source: Training, slides 17–20 (German).

title: Migrating to a new tool version
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
To continue an existing project in a newer PEExcel version, transfer saved variants through a project export file. This preserves your inputs while allowing you to benefit from improvements and fixes. Moving to the current released version is often useful before a new work phase. The download page lists versions and release notes.
This guide first exports variants from the old workbook, then imports them into the new version.1 Keep the old workbook: it retains the previous editing and calculation state for comparison.
crumbs: Migrating to a new tool version

title: Migrating to a new tool version
text:
1. Open variant management
Open the project in the old version. If you recently changed inputs, first save them as a variant using Aktuelle Eingabe speichern. Check project and variant names so you can identify the desired state later.
Click Varianten in Projekt-Varianten to choose which saved variants to transfer.






Figure 1: “Varianten” opens saved project states; “Aktuelle Eingabe speichern” first saves current inputs.
crumbs: Migrating to a new tool version

title: Migrating to a new tool version
text:
2. Export the required variants
Tick each variant to transfer in Varianten. Two are selected in the example. Click als .xlsx exportieren (export as .xlsx) to export the selection. Use Alle exportieren (export all) for all saved variants.
Save the export where you can find it easily. Include project name and date in the filename to identify its state.






Figure 2: Tick the required variants and choose “als .xlsx exportieren”; “Alle exportieren” exports every variant.
crumbs: Migrating to a new tool version

title: Migrating to a new tool version
section: 3. Import the project into the new version
text:
3. Import the project into the new version
Download the desired released version from downloads, save it as a separate working file and open it in Excel. Keep old and new workbooks separately.
In the new workbook, click Projekt-Datei importieren in Projekt-Varianten, select the saved .xlsx export and follow the import notices.






Figure 3: Start the transfer in the new workbook with “Projekt-Datei importieren”.




Select project variants and PV profiles
In Projekt-Import: Varianten Wählen, select the variants to import and click Nur ausgewählte Varianten importieren (import selected variants only). Use Alle importieren (import all) for the full list.
If PV-Import: Varianten wählen appears, select the offered PV profiles your project needs, or import all offered profiles. Check their assignment to project variants afterwards.









Figure 4: Select project variants and import the selected entries.











Figure 5: Select the PV profiles needed, or import all offered profiles.








Complete the import
Import abgeschlossen confirms completion. The tool then asks whether to close the opened project export file. Ja (yes) closes that source file; Nein (no) leaves it open, for example for inspection. Continue working in the new tool workbook.






Figure 6: Import complete: the question concerns closing the imported project file.





Simulate imported variants
The next question is Sollen die importierten Varianten jetzt simuliert werden? (Simulate imported variants now?). Choose Ja to calculate. Simulation is required to display results. Nein postpones calculation; run it later through variant management before evaluating results.






Figure 7: After importing, you can simulate the variants immediately. Calculation is required to display results.



Screenshots show a supplied development version and example dialogs. Export and import views use different example projects. Labels and dialogs may differ by version. Click to enlarge.
crumbs: Migrating to a new tool version

title: Migrating to a new tool version
section: 4. Check the transferred project and recalculate
text:
4. Check the transferred project and recalculate
Load an imported variant and inspect inputs, especially new or changed parameters. If you use custom weather or PV profiles, check that they exist in the new tool and are assigned correctly. This ensures the next calculation uses the intended project state.
If you postponed simulation or corrected inputs, calculate now with the new version. Compare results with the previous state. Repeat for other variants you intend to use. Save the new workbook and record the version used.
crumbs: Migrating to a new tool version

title: Migrating to a new tool version
text:
Why results may change
A new version may include fixes, different defaults or changes to calculation and methodology. Results may therefore change for the same transferred project. First verify identical inputs and profiles, then consult release notes.
Use newly calculated results for further work. Keep previous results in the old workbook for comparison. Do not copy calculation sheets between versions: the new workbook must use its own consistent formulas and data structures.
See managing variants for organising project states and quality assurance for subsequent verification.

Energy performance certificate
Transfer building and envelope properties from project documents. Align reference areas, uses, component areas and units with the certificate. Aggregating multiple buildings requires documented consolidation; sums and specific indicators are not interchangeable.
Workflow: Record source and version → align reference areas → transfer intended properties → check envelope and demand plausibility → save variant.

Weather
The dataset must match the location and study objective. The training names Helios-PC as a data source; the repository contains additional weather files. In future-weather comparisons, document assessment requirements separately.
Where in PEExcel? 🌦 Wetter stores data; 🏙 Quartier selects the dataset.
Workflow: Record location and weather year → check hourly sequence and completeness → transfer into the intended weather area → check the calculation. Keep weather unchanged when isolating a system measure.

section: Data for concept comparison and validation
text:
Data for concept comparison and validation








Dataset

For each input, record source, period and status: measured, planned or assumed. Time series need a common calendar, an agreed time zone and documented gap treatment. Aggregate finer measurements for hourly comparison while preserving short-term peaks as separate information.

title: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
Use PEExcel to compare supply concepts at district scale: how do heat pumps, district heating, FreeCooling or heat recovery change heat and electricity balances? Inputs describe usable capacities, efficiencies and supply shares. They support concept assessment, rather than detailed design of individual systems or their controls.
crumbs: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation

title: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation
text:
Heating
Heating demand is met in a fixed order: system 1 → 2 → 3 → 4. Systems 1 and 3 are electric; systems 2 and 4 are thermal, with a selectable energy carrier. Each system contributes within its capacity limit, passing residual demand to the next. The room-side heat-emission system additionally limits total heat delivery.
These four positions primarily allow base and peak loads to be arranged appropriately. They do not represent an arbitrarily controlled multivalent plant with freely optimised dispatch.

Example: district heating for base load, electricity for peaks
Set system 1 capacity to zero. Select district heating for system 2 and limit its capacity to the desired base load. System 3 represents direct electric peak heating with a heat-to-electricity generation efficiency of 1:1. Leave system 4 unused. District heating then meets demand up to its limit; electric heating supplies the remainder where its capacity and the emission system permit.


Reading the input blocks






Figure 1: Heating inputs: 1 first electric system, 2 subsequent systems in fixed order, 3 room-side emission and temperature setpoint. The screenshot shows a different configuration from the district-heating example.




Generation and energy input: Enter maximum heating capacity and efficiency. For heat pumps, Wirkungsgrad Erzeugung represents the seasonal performance factor: 450% in the screenshot means 4.5 units of heat per unit of electricity. Distribution losses represent heat lost on the way to use. The auxiliary-electricity share of electric systems relates to their required electrical drive energy, not total heat demand.
Additional generators: Select carriers and capacity limits so the fixed order represents your concept. Unused systems have no available capacity. Check the reference quantity for auxiliary energy for each system; the statement about electric drive energy cannot be applied generally to thermal generators.
Room-side limit: The emission system and its maximum capacity limit usable heat delivery. The minimum room-temperature setpoint defines the heating temperature level. Also check the heating season.

Calculate and compare heat demand, energy carriers and electricity demand on the results sheet to see the effects of base-load and peak-load assumptions.






NoteNo project values yet? Start with standard cases






Heating system: For a planned air-to-water heat pump, start with Wärmepumpe (Luft-Wasser). Check supply temperature, capacity and efficiency.
Heating period: Choose a time restriction matching operation; the table also includes Keine (none) and Immer (always).
Heating and cooling emission: For underfloor heating, start with Fußbodenheizung and check capacity limits.

Check the applied values for your project. How to apply presets.
crumbs: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation

title: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation
text:
Cooling
Actively cooled floor-area shares are assigned by use. The thermal model distinguishes actively cooled and non-actively cooled zones with no heat exchange between them. FreeCooling and subsequent cooling systems serve the actively cooled areas.

What FreeCooling means here
FreeCooling represents additionally available cooling for which no chiller energy is assumed in the model. It may come from different sources and configurations, such as cool water. No detailed plant model is required: enter the available cooling potential as a maximum capacity.
FreeCooling does not mean that no electricity is needed. Use the auxiliary-electricity share to account for pumps, for example. This share relates to FreeCooling output. How much potential reaches the rooms is limited by cooling demand and room-side capacity; detailed source simulation and plant control are not represented.






Figure 2: Cooling inputs: 1 FreeCooling potential and auxiliary electricity, 2 subsequent cooling systems, 3 room-side capacity and setpoint.




FreeCooling: Set available capacity and its auxiliary-electricity share.
Further cooling systems: Select energy carriers, capacity and efficiency. For electric cooling, delivered cooling relates to electricity input. Enter distribution losses and auxiliary electricity separately.
Room-side delivery: Check the emission system, maximum room-side cooling capacity and maximum room-temperature setpoint. Define the months during which cooling is available.







WarningCaution



Window-based night cooling applies to areas without active cooling. The model cannot apply active cooling and additional window night cooling to the same floor-area share. A district can contain both in different areas.


After calculation, evaluate the actively cooled zone’s heat balance and cooling electricity. For example, compare variants with and without available FreeCooling potential.






NoteNo project values yet? Start with standard cases






Cooling period: Choose a period matching the intended use.
Cooling system: Several standard cases cover reversible heat pumps, including a configuration with a FreeCooling share.
Cooled uses: If only non-residential areas should be cooled, check Kühlung in Nicht-Wohn-Nutzungen (cooling in non-residential uses).

Check the applied values for your project. How to apply presets.
crumbs: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation

title: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation
text:
Domestic hot water
Two hot-water systems can be assigned through use-specific shares. For example, a heat pump may supply apartments while instantaneous electric heaters supply offices. Assign the corresponding shares to each use and check generator parameters.
Generation, distribution and storage are separate inputs. Hot-water heat demand describes the heat required; final-energy input also depends on efficiency and losses. Check energy carrier, generation efficiency, distribution and storage losses, and auxiliary electricity for both systems. Check storage size and temperature level as well. Configure flexible temperature increases separately under storage and flexibility.






NoteNo project values yet? Start with standard cases






Hot-water demand: klimaaktiv Deklaration provides values for declaration use. The OIB selections are explicitly marked as not yet populated in the export.
Hot-water system: Choose a suitable generator as a starting point and check assignments to individual uses.

Check the applied values for your project. How to apply presets.
crumbs: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation

title: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation
text:
Ventilation
For each use, define the floor-area shares ventilated mechanically and naturally through windows. These shares divide the use into areas. 50% mechanical and 50% window ventilation means two equally sized subareas, not two complete air changes in the same area.
Both types implement the air-change rate and temporal profile specified in the use profile. To account for additional air exchange from inefficient ventilation or extra window opening, choose a corresponding air-change assumption. Dividing floor area alone does not increase air exchange.






Figure 3: Ventilation inputs: 1 mechanical and natural shares, 2 winter and summer heat-recovery values, 3 window positions for night cooling.




Assign shares: Check the mechanically ventilated share for each use and the remaining window-ventilated share. The district floor-area share indicates the weight of each use in the project.
Set heat recovery: The winter and summer values specify the recoverable share of heat in mechanically exchanged air. The tool interpolates sinusoidally between these seasonal values. They describe an annual pattern, not two independent systems. Identical values keep the share constant.
Window night cooling: Set window position and air-change rate for the intended areas. Natural-ventilation assignment must agree with the separation from actively cooled areas.

After calculation, check ventilation heat losses, heating and cooling demand, and ventilation electricity. Variant comparisons show how changes in heat recovery affect both the heat balance and supply-system demand.






NoteNo project values yet? Start with standard cases






Mechanical ventilation: Standard cases include heat recovery; check winter and summer values.
Mechanically ventilated uses: If only non-residential areas are mechanically ventilated, start with Mechanische Lüftung in Nicht-Wohn-Nutzungen (mechanical ventilation in non-residential uses).
Night cooling: Single-sided and cross ventilation are available for housing. Check openings and usable areas.

Check the applied values for your project. How to apply presets.



The annotated screenshots show example configurations from a development version supplied by the project team. Their values are not general design recommendations. Click images to enlarge.1

title: Analysing flexibility
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
When energy is used changes a district’s impact. The hourly annual simulation shows how buildings, hot water, batteries and EVs respond to PV surpluses and external enable signals. Annual indicators show the overall effect; hourly profiles explain it.
Configure inputs · Open hourly profiles · Compare variants

title: Analysing flexibility
text:
Setting up a comparison

Where in PEExcel?

Save a reference variant with documented storage and flexibility settings.
On 🔋 Flexibilität und Speicher, initially change one measure: temperature band, battery capacity or C-rate. EV settings are on 🚗 Mobilität.
Recalculate and save the measure variant. Keep weather, areas, PV and uses unchanged to isolate the measure.
Compare annual balances on 🔎 var Variantenvergleich.
On 📈 Dashboard, compare the same winter and summer weeks: read demand, supply, temperatures and states of charge together.


For multiple parameter levels, such as three storage sizes and two C-rates, calculate prepared variants by batch. This evaluates selected combinations; it does not automatically search for a global optimum.

title: Analysing flexibility
section: Research example: using hours with lower emissions
text:
Research example: using hours with lower emissions
The Quartier 4 case study investigates thermal flexibility with a heat pump and thermally activated building components, supplemented by a stationary battery and bidirectional EV use. Building demand, PV generation, uses and mobility demand remain unchanged. Emission factors, enable signals and storage options vary.
The monthly-assessed reference 23M already uses thermal flexibility and a wind-peak signal. 23H 48-10 uses hourly emission factors and enables flexible use when the current factor is at least 10% below the mean of the next 48 hours. This foresight is a case-study assumption; practical control would need forecasts.









Variant
Change in operational emissions balance relative to 23M
Change in electricity imports
Effective emissions intensity of imports




23M: monthly factors, thermal flexibility
Reference
Reference
188.9 g CO₂e/kWh


23H 48-10: hourly factors and GHG signal
−9.0%
+0.9%
160.6 g CO₂e/kWh


Plus stationary battery
−10.4%
+2.3%
154.2 g CO₂e/kWh


Plus stationary battery and bidirectional EV use
−10.0%
+5.1%
151.3 g CO₂e/kWh



Source: Schneider et al. (2025), section 3.3, table 9. The operational emissions balance includes the paper’s B6–D2 life-cycle assessment; electricity imports are annual values. Relative changes are taken from the paper.



Quartier 4 research example: annual electricity contributions and effective emissions intensities for different factors, signals and storage options. Original figure 11 from Schneider et al. (2025).


The result: Lower emissions do not necessarily require lower electricity imports. Storage losses and additional charging can increase imports while shifting use to lower-emission hours improves assessed climate impact. Additional EV use does not achieve the lowest operational emissions balance here, even though import intensity falls further.
Assessment factors and control signals change together. Differences therefore cannot be attributed solely to storage. The paper sometimes calls the last variant V2G; here, the described supply to the building or district is termed bidirectional EV use.

title: Analysing flexibility
section: What to check in hourly profiles
text:
What to check in hourly profiles

Enablement and charging: Does additional use actually occur during enabled hours?
Comfort: Do room temperatures remain within the chosen band?
Storage use: Does useful discharge follow charging, or do losses and high residual charge dominate?
Grid exchange: Are imports and feed-in shifted in time? A better GHG balance does not prove a lower grid peak.
Annual effect: How do self-consumption, imports, losses, full cycles and GHG balance change together?

The simulation resolves the year hourly. Subhourly peaks, grid voltages and transformer loading require finer or additional analysis.

Declaration: This research example illustrates temporal assessment. Verification uses prescribed factors and assumptions; research variants do not replace them.

Publication: Declaration-Ready Climate-Neutral PEDs, section 3.3 · Indicators and boundaries · Mobility behaviour

title: Examples
text:
Heat balance
Transmission and ventilation losses, night ventilation and cooling demand are compared with solar/internal gains and heating demand. Contributions are annual energy per net floor area. All three heat balances close within numerical precision.




Heat balance of three variants.

title: Examples
text:
Final-energy balance
All three variants are entirely electrically supplied; exported district-heating, natural-gas, biomass and other-carrier contributions are zero. The chart shows electrical final energy for local use, including building services, user electricity, storage charging and district EV charging.
Direct/flexible PV use, conventional/signal-controlled imports and available discharge flows provide supply. Feed-in and external EV charging are outside this local-use balance. This prevents counting them as local demand coverage; all three balances close.




Electrical final-energy balance of local use.


Interactive HTML · SVG · PNG · Results CSV

title: Examples
text:
Primary-energy balance
Assessment includes demand, substitution equivalents and context factors. The difference between supply and demand sides is an assessment result, not an error in a physically closed balance. Flexibility and context contributions are not additional physical generation.




Primary-energy balance of three variants.


Interactive HTML · SVG · PNG · Results CSV

title: Examples
text:
GHG balance
The figure covers exported life-cycle contributions for 2025–2075: construction, building services and vehicles (EE), and building operation and mobility (OE). Negative contributions, notably feed-in and mobility-boundary effects, retain their signs. The diamond marks the exported total, equal to the sum of displayed components.
The reference is gross, not net, floor area. GWP100 describes climate-impact assessment and is distinct from the 50-year study period. L1–L3 reference bands do not replace verification. PV LCA can be modelled but is excluded by the klimaaktiv method and is zero in these exports.




Life-cycle GHG balance of three variants.


Interactive HTML · SVG · PNG · Results CSV

title: Examples
text:
Result checks and provenance
Result tables and input comparison · Numerical balance checks CSV · Executable Python workflow
The analysis uses saved exports; no Excel simulation is rerun. Figures record source file, scenario, version and source checksum. They do not establish confirmed declaration status.
Time-resolved electrical flows are shown separately for Aspern F7. Completeness of hourly exports for the three refurbishment variants is being checked for a future extension.

title: Examples
text:
Aspern F7: time-resolved electrical flows
Aspern PVCheck _ F7.xlsx contains 8,760 hourly values on the 2018 timeline. Charts show conventional imports, direct PV use, flexible PV use where nonzero, and PV feed-in. Imports include conventional components grouped under E_grid in the schema.
Boundary: These are selected flow profiles, not a closed consumption balance. Consumption, storage and complete signal-controlled import channels are absent from this export. Missing quantities are not treated as zero.

Seasonal mean daily profiles
The four seasons derive from exported calendar information. Each hour of day shows the average over all corresponding hours in the season. Values are mean power in W/m² net floor area, calculated from hourly Wh/m² after verifying a one-hour interval. Seasonal means are not actual daily profiles.




Aspern F7 seasonal electrical flow profiles.


Full-size interactive HTML · SVG · PNG


Chronological hourly values
January and July weeks are directly selectable windows. Zoom, range selection and legend controls support analysis of individual contributions. These weeks provide orientation; they are not statistically representative samples. Positive values represent local PV use and conventional imports, negative values PV feed-in.

The existing interactive view remains separately available. Chart labels and controls are reused unchanged.

title: Comparing variants
text:
Interpreting balances together
Envelope quality changes heat demand; PV changes generation and supply timing; flexible building services and storage shift imports. Mobility measures affect an additional boundary. Read combined effects from the calculated package, not by simply adding isolated improvements.
Primary-energy charts also include context contributions. These are assessment quantities, not additional physical generation.

title: Comparing variants
section: Example: storage capacity and charging power
text:
Example: storage capacity and charging power
Save a reference without a stationary battery and variants with 10 and 20 kWh. For each capacity, test C-rates of 0.5 and 1 h⁻¹. Keep PV, weather, uses and comfort band unchanged. Resulting powers are 5, 10, 10 and 20 kW.
Compare self-consumption, autonomy, imports, peak feed-in, losses, full cycles and GHG balance. These numbers illustrate an experiment, not a sizing recommendation. Hourly profiles explain whether larger capacity is used or power is the main limitation.

title: Life-cycle assessment
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
Climate-neutral PED assessment extends beyond operational energy. Embodied building emissions and operational greenhouse gas emissions are assessed over a defined study period.

title: Life-cycle assessment
text:
Distinguishing three time concepts







Term
Meaning




Study period
Balance period: 50 years, 2025–2075


Target year
Policy or methodological climate target, such as 2040 or 2050; not the balance end date


Decarbonisation pathway
Evolution of energy-system emission factors, affecting future operational energy



A cumulative presentation integrates contributions over time. It is neither a single annual balance nor automatic proof of achieving a national climate target. Reduction pathways and budget rules belong to the assessment method.

title: Life-cycle assessment
section: GHG reduction pathways and life cycle
text:
GHG reduction pathways and life cycle



GHG reduction pathways to 2050 for different energy carriers. Source: PEExcel training.


The method uses 2025–2075 and sectoral decarbonisation pathways to 2050. Decarbonised systems after 2050 are an assessment assumption. The training’s budget of 320 kg CO₂eq/m² gross floor area is a cumulative reference, not an annual emissions rate.



Cumulative emissions from construction, operation and refurbishment, and biogenic storage. Source: PEExcel training.


The timing of emissions, refurbishment and biogenic storage affects the life-cycle balance. Credits in the diagram are methodological assumptions, not universally transferable material properties.



Operational-emissions boundary: imports, local PV use and feed-in. Original English figure from PEExcel training, slides 22–23 and 31.


Training source (German).

title: Life-cycle assessment
text:
Components, operation and budget
Assign constructions and quantities transparently. Interpret embodied and operational contributions together with boundary, period and budget. The variant comparison shows exported life-cycle results, including negative assessment contributions.

Declaration — PV LCA: Embodied PV manufacturing emissions can be modelled, but the klimaaktiv assessment method does not include them. An input or result does not automatically mean a contribution enters the declaration. Do not generalise this to other systems or methods.

title: Life-cycle assessment
text:
Entering LCA inputs
Location: ☁ THG → Baulich (construction).

Where in PEExcel?

Under Baulich, select constructions or a preset and check quantities.
Add grouped measures or an overall LCA input without counting existing measures twice.
Assign fossil and biogenic contributions and service life until replacement transparently.
Under Technische Gebäudeausstattung (building services), enter relevant systems and reference quantities; align vehicle manufacturing with mobility settings.
Recalculate and check construction and operational contributions together on the results sheet.


Component assignment connects geometry, quantities and life-cycle balance. A geometric area alone is not a complete LCA assignment. Construction, boundary conditions and use must be traceable.



Component types assigned in a building section.


The original figure adds situations beyond the simplified schematic sections. Click to enlarge. Source: docs/ComponentTypes.png; see training, slides 13–14.

title: Life-cycle assessment
text:
Project workflow

Assign areas and components according to actual construction.
Distinguish outdoor air, ground, heated and unheated adjacent spaces.
Check quantities and units before importing LCA properties.
Document unshown elements such as balconies, columns and window frames separately.
Check adopted component values and assessment boundary.







NoteResearch / Expert





In the second reference model, the basement ceiling separates heated from unheated space and forms the thermal boundary. The internal floor slab is also an assessed construction component but is not an external thermal boundary there. Thermal and life-cycle balances examine different properties of the same component.

Connecting to Eco2soft

Where in PEExcel? Create the appropriate assessment in Eco2soft and export CSV. Align system boundary, reference area, units, fossil/biogenic contributions and replacement assumptions before transfer. After importing, check which components or aggregate results were adopted and review existing inputs for double counting.

Check field mapping in the CSV import dialog. Different boundaries or already recorded components can otherwise cause missing contributions or double counting.

title: Verification and declaration
text:
Preparing verification

Version and objective: Document tool version, quality level and project boundary.
Evidence for inputs: Record sources for areas, energy certificate, weather, PV, mobility and component data.
Declaration values: Identify differing model assumptions and apply verification requirements.
Calculate and check: Review results and AUDIT; address errors and notices.
Assessment boundary: Distinguish physical flows, virtual context contributions and assessed emissions.
Save documentation: Keep variant, export, calculation state and verification documents together.

AUDIT supports quality assurance. This website performs no separate eligibility check. Official contacts in the documentation can address verification questions.
Manual · Training, slides 34–35 · Contact

title: Verification and declaration
text:
Verification sheets
Where in PEExcel? PEQ (positive energy district), PEQ+M (PED with mobility) and KN PEQ (climate-neutral PED).

Ribbon: klimaaktiv PEQ → Nachweise → PEQ im Betrieb / PEQ mit Mobilität / Klimaneutrales PEQ

The sheets summarise project value, target or budget, and difference for each boundary. PEQ covers operation; PEQ+M adds motorised private transport; KN PEQ additionally covers life-cycle GHG assessment. Outputs support verification documentation but do not replace professional review.

title: Verification and declaration
text:
Quality assurance
For verification, align entered areas and use shares with project documents. Also check calculated net floor areas, volumes and floor-area ratio. Document the sources so model and submitted project version can be traced.
Where in PEExcel? AUDIT (quality assurance).
AUDIT supports automated plausibility checks, showing deviations from predefined declaration values for the current variant. A deviation need not be a modelling error; review it for verification and justify it in the audit report. Justification alone does not replace professional acceptance of a deviation.

Where in PEExcel? Save project/variant name, tool version and calculation state. Check data sources and boundaries; address AUDIT notices individually. Apply mandatory requirements or clarify deviations professionally. File results and export with verification documentation.

Source: Training, slides 4 and 35 (German).

title: Thermal envelope and heat flows
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
The model distinguishes an actively cooled zone and a zone without active cooling, thermally decoupled from one another.1
Solar gains enter through windows; internal heat gains arise inside the room. Transmission and ventilation are shown as examples of heat removal; their actual direction depends on conditions.

title: Thermal envelope and heat flows
text:
Entering building-physics inputs
Describe the areas and properties of components that determine the district’s heat exchange. The interactive view helps distinguish the thermal boundary from component assignment.

Where in PEExcel? Open 🧱 Bauphysik (building physics).


Inputs on the building-physics sheet







Input group
Assignment




Opaque thermal envelope
External walls excluding windows, roof or uppermost thermal ceiling, basement ceiling/ground-contact floor; areas and U-values


Translucent components
Window areas including frames by orientation, U-values and g-values


Thermal bridges / airtightness
Allowance and n50 assumption based on project information


Shading / movable solar protection
Reduction factors and control assumptions; distinguish suggested values from values actually applied


Effective thermal mass
Construction type and effective heat capacity



Apply presets, then check project-specific areas and properties. After calculation, check the heat balance on the results sheet.

Declaration: Internal heat gains and user electricity can in principle be modelled freely. For a declaration, use the designated values of the tool version in use.

The section view uses a schematic reference building.

title: Thermal envelope and heat flows
text:
Footnotes


Each zone uses a simplified thermal RC model with one thermal mass: heat capacity C represents storage, and resistances R represent heat exchange. No heat exchange is assumed between the two zones. The model supports energy concept assessment; it is not a detailed multi-zone room model. Explanation by the project team; PEExcel training, slides 11–14 (German).↩︎

title: Excel dashboard
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
The dashboard shows hourly energy flows and storage states. A common time window lets you examine demand, supply and storage response together. The Python scenario explorer is a separate application.

title: Excel dashboard
section: Selecting a period and hourly profiles
text:
Selecting a period and hourly profiles

Where in PEExcel?

Select a period under Datum auswählen; use the timeline for contiguous ranges.
Choose a manageable window, such as one week. TAGE in the screenshot sets the date window; it is not itself evidence of hourly aggregation.
Check chart time axes: hourly profiles must show timestamps within days.
After recalculation, use Aktualisieren (refresh) so pivot views adopt the new results.





Period selection and refresh above the dynamic charts. Hourly timestamps in the January/February window accompany electricity demand, supply and storage states.

title: Excel dashboard
text:
Electricity demand and use
The top chart shows user electricity, inflexible building-services demand, EV charging and additional flexible use. Read storage charging as a separate contribution. Compare power-profile peaks with enabled periods and storage states.

title: Excel dashboard
text:
Electricity supply
The second chart distinguishes conventional and flexible imports, PV use, battery withdrawal, EV discharge and PV feed-in. Use each legend to identify simultaneous contributions; respect signs and boundaries.

title: Excel dashboard
section: Room temperature and thermal building mass
text:
Room temperature and thermal building mass
Temperatures of cooled and uncooled areas show thermal response. Check flexible preconditioning against setpoints and permitted temperature bands. Temperature is a state indicator, not stored energy in kWh.

title: Excel dashboard
text:
Hot-water storage
States of hot-water systems 1 and 2 show charging and use during the selected period. Read percentages according to the chart scale; do not interpret them as temperature or absolute storage capacity.

title: Excel dashboard
text:
EVs and battery
EV-SoC shows charge levels by use; Batterie-SoC shows stationary storage. Assess minimum charge, flexible charging and discharging alongside electricity flows.

title: Excel dashboard
section: Thermal daily averages and further views
text:
Thermal daily averages and further views
Heat gains and losses of the two thermally decoupled zones are also evaluated as daily averages. Daily averages and hourly power are different aggregations.



Model and dashboard: thermally decoupled zones, heat balance and daily-average heat flows. The lower chart explicitly shows daily means.


Flexibility analysis · Mobility behaviour · Storage parameters · Results sheet · Aspern F7 website profiles
Website profiles use exported channels. A missing export channel does not mean the quantity is absent from the Excel dashboard.
Source: Training, slides 11 and 32 (German).

title: Getting started with PEExcel
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
PEExcel is the calculation and verification tool for the klimaaktiv standard for positive energy districts. It connects building operation, energy supply, motorised private mobility and life-cycle emissions in an hourly assessment model.
Use Excel to investigate and calculate project variants, compare their energy and greenhouse gas balances, and prepare the evidence for a declaration.

title: Getting started with PEExcel
text:
The workflow at a glance
Work follows a recurring sequence:



Model → calculate → evaluate → save variant


Starting from a project description, define inputs and measures, calculate and check results. Then adjust variants and compare them.

title: Getting started with PEExcel
section: Five steps to your first evaluation
text:
Five steps to your first evaluation

1. Download and open the Excel tool
Download the current Excel tool, save it locally and open it in Microsoft Excel. Enable macros for advanced operation and variant functions. Keep an unchanged starting file for your own projects.


2. Define the project and baseline variant

Where in PEExcel? Sheet ▶ (Quick Start).
Select the basic project and geometry parameters. Alternatively, load a saved variant.

Quick Start provides quick access to the main model settings.



Quick Start with thematic input sheets and quick selection. Supplied v1_12 view dated 24 June 2026; example values are not project requirements.




3. Set the configuration
Choose suitable presets, for example for the envelope, heating system or PV. Presets apply several related parameters together. Check whether the resulting inputs suit your project. Make project-specific changes on the relevant technical sheets.


4. Calculate and check results

Where in PEExcel?

Trigger calculation with F9.
Open 📊 Erg (Ergebnisse) and check annual balances.
Check primary-energy and GHG balances.
If needed, use 📈 (Dashboard) for hourly evaluations.


In manual calculation mode, results are only up to date after recalculation.


5. Save and compare the variant
Save the project state as a clearly named variant. Change individual measures, recalculate and compare results in the variant comparison.

title: Getting started with PEExcel
text:
Where next?

Finding your way around Excel: understand sheets, colours and input fields.
Modelling: edit project parameters and technical systems in detail.
Verification: data quality, declaration values and quality assurance.

For existing projects, migration describes transferring inputs between versions.
Source: PEExcel training, especially slides 3, 7–8 and 24–30 (German).

Model


BGF / GFA
Gross floor area; GFA_total is modelled GFA. The indicator’s unit identifies the applicable area.
Model


Energy / power
Energy is a quantity, e.g. kWh; power is an energy flow, e.g. kW. An hourly kWh value over exactly one hour equals mean kW, not instantaneous peak power.
Time resolution


Specific annual value
For example kWh/(m² NFA·a): annual energy per NFA. The schema often writes kWh/m²NGFa.
Indicators


Final energy
Energy of the carriers used within the relevant boundary, before primary-energy assessment.
Annual balances


Primary energy
Energy assessed using conversion factors. Note context contributions separately; final-energy kWh and primary-energy kWh are different quantities.
Assessment


Demand / supply
Different sides of a balance; meaning depends on system and report.
Reading results


Context factor
Methodological contribution for density, mobility or refurbishment, not physical generation.
Standard and method





PV, flexibility and storage



Term
Meaning and limits
Further reading




PV self-consumption
PV energy used locally; the share refers to PV generation. Direct and flexible use may be separate.
PV


Energy autonomy / self-supply
Local PV use relative to modelled electricity demand, distinct from self-consumption share or supply security.
Indicators


Flexibility
Shifting flows in time within technical and use-related limits.
Analysis


State of charge / SoC
Stored energy or share of available capacity. Check the variable’s representation and unit.
Systems


C-rate
Charge/discharge power divided by capacity: 0.5 h⁻¹ at 20 kWh equals 10 kW.
Systems


Round-trip efficiency / RTE
Energy delivered divided by energy absorbed over a storage cycle or evaluation period. The catalogue shows the unit actually stored in the schema.
Flexibility


Equivalent full cycles
Energy throughput relative to capacity according to the indicator definition. Partial cycles may sum to one full cycle.
Analysis





Costs and climate impact
The catalogue includes costs for grid import, flexible import and feed-in, plus a cost total. Existing OUT definitions are not a complete economic model. Check tariffs, signs, period and included cost components for each project. Missing schema information is explicitly identified below.



Term
Meaning and reference quantity
Further reading




THG / GWP
Greenhouse gas impact in CO₂ equivalents; period and area reference are part of the indicator.
Climate impact


Operational emissions / OE
Emissions from assessed operational flows, dependent on factors and decarbonisation pathways.
GHG balance


Embodied emissions / EE
Emissions of assessed materials, constructions and systems; included life-cycle contributions follow the method.
LCA


Life cycle / LCA
Assessment over the defined period. Cumulative kg CO₂e/m² is not directly comparable with annual kg CO₂e/(m²·a).
Method


Decarbonisation pathway
Change in assumed emission factors over time.
Climate impact





Finding your way around the tool







Term
Meaning in the workflow




PEQ / PED
Positive energy district with a defined boundary and quality level.


Variant / scenario
Documented assumptions and associated saved results.


Thermal envelope / zone
Envelope: boundary of the thermally assessed space. Zone: area grouped in the thermal model.


User electricity
Electricity demand arising from use; designated requirements apply to declarations.


Declaration value / AUDIT
Mandatory declaration value, or tool-assisted checking of relevant inputs and deviations.


IN / OUT
Input and result tables. OUT also contains auxiliary quantities, not only independent KPIs.


SIM2
Hourly export, separate from OUT results. The catalogues do not show SIM time-series channels.



Find Excel sheets · Prepare verification

title: Terms, parameters and indicators
text:
Input parameters
The IN catalogue shows every input variable defined in the active schema. Open a domain or search by term or variable name. Domain and Entity Group further narrow results. The two catalogues filter independently.
The interactive catalogues below are reused unchanged in German, including labels, units, emojis from the icon field and metadata. Emojis aid assignment; missing icons are not invented. Domain headings provide orientation while original keys remain visible.
Metadaten anzeigen (show metadata) reveals measure type (measure), Entity Group, Entity Key, spatial/temporal reference and additional description where recorded. The catalogue contains definitions, not current input values, defaults or validation of permissible values. Each variable has a shareable link.

title: Terms, parameters and indicators
text:
Output indicators
Open a domain or search across variables. German labels, units and metadata are taken unchanged from the active Python schema. A schema entry establishes that a variable is defined, not that it exists, is populated or is meaningful in every export or scenario.
Metadaten anzeigen shows measure type, Entity Group, Entity Key, spatial/temporal reference and additional description where available. Version information helps align with your Excel export. Indicator links can be shared individually.

512 OUT-Variablen aus Schema 1_13_1_dev.
Vollständiger Definitionsbestand, keine Projektwerte. Auch Hilfsgrößen sind enthalten.

36 ohne Einheit, 16 ohne deutsches Label und
512 ohne zusätzliche Beschreibung. „Nicht hinterlegt“ bedeutet nicht „dimensionslos“.

title: Designing districts for the future
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
For professional competence partners, designers, consultants, researchers and students: PEExcel combines Excel with hourly simulation, traceable assessment methods and a Python interface. Developed by the Climate-fit Buildings and Districts research group at UAS Technikum Wien.

title: Designing districts for the future
text:
What you can investigate


📊

Compare variants


Assess individual measures and packages with consistent boundaries. Compare variants →



🔋

Use flexibility


Investigate building mass, hot water, batteries and EVs hour by hour. Analyse flexibility →



🚗

Include mobility


Understand presence, charging and travel demand by use and season. Analyse mobility →

title: Designing districts for the future
section: Connecting annual balances and hourly profiles
text:
Connecting annual balances and hourly profiles
Annual balances show how much energy is needed and supplied. Hourly simulation shows when PV, demand and storage coincide. This lets you assess self-consumption, imports, storage losses and comfort together. Primary-energy and life-cycle GHG assessment complement physical flows.
Results and indicators · Hourly Excel dashboard · Model and inputs

title: Designing districts for the future
section: Three levels of the positive-energy standard
text:
Three levels of the positive-energy standard

Positive energy district: building operational energy and district-related supply.
Positive energy district with mobility: additionally, motorised private transport energy.
Climate-neutral positive energy district: additionally, life-cycle GHG emissions, especially embodied building emissions.




Overview of the three assessment levels.


Standard and background · What counts for a declaration?

title: Designing districts for the future
text:
Project comparison and time-resolved analysis
The three refurbishment variants show heat, final-energy, primary-energy and GHG balances on a common data basis. Aspern F7 adds seasonal daily profiles and chronological hourly series.
The schematic building section distinguishes component assignment, thermal boundaries and qualitative heat flows.
Methodology and research · Download Excel · Python interface · Python batch simulation (German)

Declaration: Custom assumptions can be modelled. A klimaaktiv declaration requires the declaration values and assessment rules of the relevant version. PV LCA can be modelled but is not included in the klimaaktiv assessment method.
