title: Analysing mobility behaviour
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
Parking periods determine when EVs can absorb and supply energy. PEExcel connects hourly presence and travel demand with PV, charging infrastructure and other district demand. Comparing uses and seasons shows where flexible charging is effective.
Mobility model and inputs · Excel dashboard · Flexibility

title: Analysing mobility behaviour
text:
Comparing winter and summer



Hourly mobility energy balances and EV states of charge for housing, offices, school and supermarket, from top to bottom. Winter left, summer right. Original figure 7 from Schneider and Baptista (2025).


The figure shows a winter week from 28 January to 3 February and a summer window in July. The left axis shows area-specific energy flows as mean hourly power; the right shows SoC in percent. Summer charts are on the right.







Display
How to read it




Green
Charging from local renewable sources


Yellow-green
Charging from regional, intermittently available renewable surpluses


Dark purple
Other grid charging


Pink hatching
External charging outside the district


Narrow negative bars
Energy consumed for journeys


Red/pink discharge contributions
Vehicle supply to building services or user electricity


SoC lines
Average charge levels: on site, off site and across the vehicle group



Driving energy and external charging explain the mobility balance but do not belong entirely to local electricity supply. Evaluate local charging energy separately from total attributed mobility demand.

title: Analysing mobility behaviour
text:
What the four uses show
Housing: Many vehicles are available in the evening and at night. In summer, PV-charged vehicles can later supply user electricity and systems, provided bidirectional use is enabled and minimum SoC is respected.
Offices: Daytime presence can coincide with PV generation. The effect depends on working days, parking periods and available charging power.
School: The model uses different simultaneity from offices and housing. Floor-area occupancy and statistically generated journeys must not be equated directly with a permanently present vehicle count.
Supermarket: Short stays and frequent turnover limit transferable energy per vehicle. Many different vehicles may generate charging demand although only a small share is present simultaneously.
See the mobility model for the separate presence profiles and their data basis.

title: Analysing mobility behaviour
text:
Research example: bidirectional charging
In the paper’s residential example, bidirectional charging down to an average minimum SoC of 60% reduces annual grid demand for heating and user electricity from 29.3 to 21.3 kWh/m² net floor area, about 28%. Equivalent full cycles increase from 189 to 229, about 20%.
This illustrates a trade-off between avoided imports and increased battery use. It is neither a general saving in total mobility electricity demand nor a calculation of battery life. Values apply to the investigated configuration.
Source: Schneider and Baptista (2025), results, p. 5. Residential vehicles can supply the district in this model; discharge is not assumed for every use group.

title: Analysing mobility behaviour
text:
Evaluating your own mobility variant

Where in PEExcel?

Save a reference with unchanged building, weather and PV.
On 🚗 Mobilität, change one assumption, such as EV share, charging power or bidirectional use. Document minimum charge levels and vehicle capacities.
Calculate and save a separate variant.
On 📊 Erg Ergebnisse, check local charging, external charging, mobility demand and EV full cycles.
On 📈 Dashboard, open the same winter and summer periods. Assess SoC and charging flows by use together.
On 🔎 var Variantenvergleich, compare energy and GHG effects.


A further comparison of mobility measures may change distance travelled. In that case, the causation-based mobility balance matters alongside charging flows.

title: Analysing mobility behaviour
text:
Scope and limitations
The model represents vehicle groups with average states of charge. It supports concept comparisons and investigations of the use mix. An adequate average SoC does not guarantee that every vehicle is sufficiently charged at departure. Individual charging schedules and short-term power peaks require more detailed data and models.
Publication: Annual Hourly E-Mobility Modelling and Assessment · Indicators · Managing variants

title: Modelling the district
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
PEExcel connects the physical simulation of a district with assessment of its energy and climate impacts. Describe buildings, uses and supply, calculate their interactions and compare results. These interactions are particularly useful: a larger PV system, different heat supply or change in use affects several energy flows at once.

title: Modelling the district
text:
What the simulation brings together

Operational energy model
The model connects sources, conversion, storage and uses within the district boundary. It covers space heating and cooling, domestic hot water, ventilation, auxiliary energy and user electricity. Local PV generation, storage and flexibility measures change when electricity is imported, used or exported.1



District energy model: sources, supply systems, storage and uses connected by energy flows.


The diagram helps trace a measure’s implications. A heat pump changes both heat supply and electricity demand. Its timing in turn affects PV generation and storage and flexibility. Electric mobility also adds charging demand and available storage capacity.


Life-cycle assessment
LCA extends the view from ongoing operation to emissions from construction and refurbishment, and the biogenic storage considered. Operational energy and construction measures can thus be assessed together over the study period.



Life-cycle assessment: operational energy, construction, refurbishment and biogenic storage contribute to emissions over time.


The method determines the contributions and changes over time included. The LCA page explains the study period, decarbonisation and boundaries. For example, assess operational savings together with the construction effort required to achieve them.

Where in PEExcel?

Presets and project-specific inputs
A preset is an input aid, not project-specific evidence. Its name does not describe every active setting. The actual parameter values applied are decisive.
Check technical capacities, system shares, setpoints, losses and activation switches for plausibility and agreement with the project.

Declaration: Replace examples and estimates with suitable project data. Parameters marked as declaration values are mandatory for verification, although free model variants may use different values.

title: PV inputs
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
How much of your local PV generation can the district use itself? PEExcel connects hourly generation with electricity demand, storage charging and grid feed-in. Investigate how system size and timing affect supply. For an initial model, size PV using roof area. For a specific system design, use your own externally simulated generation profile.

title: PV inputs
text:
Simplified inputs: roof-area scaling
Set PV Modus to Vereinfacht (simplified). Select a suitable generation profile, for example an east–west system. Available roof area and the proportion used for PV determine sizing. Check the resulting PV area, total capacity and yield.






Figure 1: Sizing PV: 1 mode, 2 profile and sizing, 3 available presets.




Select the mode: PV simulation and mode determine how generation is represented.
Check sizing: The profile describes generation timing. The roof-area share scales the system; the fields below show area, capacity and yield. Current inputs are decisive. After manual changes, a previously selected preset name may differ from the actual share, as the screenshot illustrates.
Get started quickly: Presets help compare roof-area shares. Start with a preset and adapt the inputs to your project.

Recalculate and check on the results sheet how much PV electricity is used directly, stored or exported. Higher annual yield alone does not tell you whether additional generation coincides with demand.

title: PV inputs
text:
Detailed inputs: hourly generation profile
If the system has been simulated specifically for the project, import its hourly profile. Document location, orientation, installed capacity and losses already included. PV-Import places standard profiles alongside Import User Profil PV.






Figure 2: Entering profiles: 1 standard profiles, 2 user-profile columns, 3 associated hourly values.




Existing profiles: The left-hand group contains profiles for different orientations and system types.
Name your profiles: Use the orange columns and assign unambiguous names.
Enter hourly values: Paste the annual series of 8,760 hours into the appropriate column. Only the first hours are shown. Check units and timing: mean hourly power in kW is numerically equal to energy in kWh over exactly one hour. Treat normalised and absolute profiles according to their reference capacity.

Select the profile on the PV sheet and check scaling and loss factors. Do not apply losses already included in the external simulation again. Weather and PV series must align in time; resolve missing hours or different calendars before importing.
Recalculate. Compare annual totals and typical daily profiles in the Excel dashboard with the external simulation to check magnitude and timing.

title: Methodology and research
text:
English translation · 5 November 2026. Original screenshots, interactive tools, catalogues and notebook outputs are shared with the German site and retain their original language.
PEExcel implements the klimaaktiv standard for climate-neutral positive energy districts in a calculation and verification tool. The standard defines quantitative primary-energy and greenhouse-gas requirements for buildings and districts. Scientific foundations, target derivation and accounting rules are detailed in the online background report (German).
PEExcel combines building operation, hourly energy flows, renewable generation, location-specific mobility, life-cycle emissions and context factors in an integrated assessment model. It supports design variants, quantitative assessment of target achievement and traceable verification.
